title: Wrap-up incident chronicle: afternoon rotation 2026-04-16
body:
Purpose: afternoon on-call wrap-up + follow-ups for the KV-prefix staleness / partial-503 case. Use this as the handoff note for the night rotation and as a place to draft runbook changes.

Summary (short):
- At ~13:10 PDT we saw elevated 95/99 latency for hosted text-generation endpoints (api.redwood/v1/generate) affecting a subset of customers using long-context chat sessions. P50 unaffected, P95/P99 spiked from baseline 120ms -> 1.3s.
- Concurrently, the routing layer reported ~2% 503s for requests routed to the primary EU-hosted pool for certain model variants (quantized-ggml-v1 and rwd-7b-q8). 503s were intermittent and correlated with cache-miss bursts.
- Root cause (working hypothesis): stale/evicted KV-prefix caches after a rolling kernel update + simultaneous aggressive batching from a new customer canary, causing memory-pressure-driven transient failures in the per-model cache manager leading to slow fallback path and occasional request cancellations.

What we saw (timeline, notes):
- 12:58 PDT: Canary deploy of kernel optimization (serving-runtime commit 8d7a9c) completed to dedicated-eu pool (automated canary rollout, step 3/4).
- 13:04 PDT: Spike in request rate from a customer (acct: deeplingo) using long sequences (avg tokens/req ~ 4k) — traffic from their session replay increased 8x for ~6 minutes.
- 13:10 PDT: Alerts fired: latency_p95 > 800ms for route /generate; error_rate > 0.5% for pool:dedicated-eu. Pager duty triggered, on-call paged.
- 13:12 PDT: I joined bridge (link in linked_artifacts). Observed logs showing frequent 'kv-cache-oom' and 'async-fallback-timeout' messages in model-worker logs.
- 13:18 PDT: Temporary mitigation: scaled up dedicated-eu pool by +2 nodes (manual scale via infra console) and increased model-worker KV-cache soft limit from 12GB -> 14GB for rwd-7b-q8. Latency improved but 503s persisted for 10–12 minutes.
- 13:36 PDT: Rolled back canary commit 8d7a9c -> 7f2b3a, which removed recent kernel changes from the pool. Immediate reduction in kv-cache OOM logs. Error rate returned to baseline by 13:48 PDT.

Actions taken (during shift):
- Manual scale: infra scaled +2 dedicated-eu nodes (notes: temporary, cost tracked in JIRA-INC-4821).
- Re-tuned cache soft-limit to reduce eviction TTLs for active sessions (temporary).
- Rolled back kernel canary from dedicated-eu pool (rollback successful).
- Contacted product infra owner (Miguel) to pause any non-critical canaries until week-of-runbook changes land.

Immediate follow-ups (must do in next 24–72h):
- Create a short postmortem draft and link to JIRA-INC-4821 (owner: Aisha). Target: initial draft 2026-04-17.
- Add a permanent guardrail in the autoscaler: disallow simultaneous canary kernel rollouts + customer-initiated large-sequence canaries in same pool (owner: infra team, assignee: Miguel).
- Add alerting refinement: split kv-cache OOM alert into (a) OOM-recoverable (soft-limit) and (b) persistent OOMs (hard-limit) so paging is more accurate. (owner: eng-sre, assignee: Rina).
- Run a chaos test: simulate high long-context traffic with cache warmup to validate eviction behavior under the proposed kernel change (owner: serving-runtime team, assignee: Evan).
- Update the runbook section "kv-cache / memory-pressure" with explicit rollback steps, thresholds, and a pre-scale checklist (owner: eng-sre).

Runbook draft notes (kv-cache memory-pressure) — inline edits to consider:
- Trigger: kv-cache-oom log count > 5 in 30s for same model-worker id OR sustained per-worker GC stalls > 200ms over 2 minutes.
- Immediate mitigation steps (ordered):
  1) Open bridge, note affected pool(s) and model id(s).
  2) Increase per-pool KV soft cache limit by +15% (quick patch); watch eviction metrics for 2 mins.
  3) If errors persist, scale pool by +1 node and re-evaluate in 3 mins.
  4) If still degraded, rollback last kernel/serving-runtime canary on that pool (do not retry kernel canaries until SRE+serving-runtime sign-off).
  5) If rollback isn't available, mark the pool as draining for new sessions and route traffic to fallback pools (note: update routing policy TTL to prefer warm caches).
- Post-incident: run a per-tenant replay to see how long sessions warmed the cache; record top 3 tenants by prefix-usage.

Customer impact + communication:
- Affected customers: three hosted customers had elevated latencies; one customer (deeplingo) saw ~2% 503s for 8 minutes. Product/CS notified via incident channel; support ticket created (SUP-9982).
- Recommended comms: short status update to affected customers explaining transient degradation due to kernel rollout causing cache pressure; no data loss. Hold on a fuller postmortem until root cause verified. (owner: customer-success, contact: Lilly Hammond).

Open questions / unknowns: (notes to self)
- Why did the kernel update change KV memory footprint? Need diff on allocator/kv manager behavior. Check PR notes on mem-layout change.
- Did the long-sequence canary cause different cache eviction patterns (LRU vs LFU) due to sequence prefix overlaps? Need trace correlation between prefix hashes and eviction churn.
- Are our eviction thresholds tuned for multi-tenant patterns? Might need dynamic per-tenant caps.

Logs / metrics pointers (quick links):
- dashboards: /dashboards/pool/dedicated-eu/kv-cache-evictions
- query: error logs filter "kv-cache-oom" in last 2 hours (use 2x window around 13:00–14:00)
- trace: sample trace IDs captured in bridge: trace-0a7b, trace-0a7c, trace-0a7e

TODOs (short checklist):
- [ ] Draft postmortem (Aisha) — due 2026-04-17
- [ ] Add guardrail ticket to infra backlog (Miguel) — due 2026-04-20
- [ ] Run chaos/scale test (Evan) — schedule by 2026-04-19
- [ ] Update runbook with explicit rollback + routing steps (Rina) — due 2026-04-18
- [ ] Customer note draft (Lilly / CS) — coordinate by EOD 2026-04-16

Misc notes / observations:
- This felt different from previous OOM incidents: logs show more frequent soft-eviction churn rather than single-worker hard OOM. Might be due to allocator fragmentation after kernel changes.
- Cost note: manual scaling consumed 2 spot capacity units for ~30 minutes. Add to JIRA-INC-4821 cost appendix.
- Proposed improvement: add a lightweight per-request circuit breaker that checks cache-hit-rate for the prefix before accepting large sequence requests; if prefix miss-rate > 60% deny large request or route to warmed fallback. (brainstorm — not final).

Handoff summary for night on-call:
- System state: normal (post-13:48). Kernel rollback done. No ongoing errors.
- Active follow-ups: postmortem draft, runbook edits, infra guardrail ticket, chaos test. See TODO list.
- If latency spikes again: first check kv-cache-oom logs + last kernel-change tag for pool; if both present, follow runbook immediate mitigation steps above and page eng-sre.

Notes to night on-call (quick):
- Bridge details in linked_artifacts. If paging on-call, escalate to Miguel (infra) then Rina (SRE).
- Don't immediately reapply recent kernel change; confirm with serving-runtime before testing.
- Keep manual scale as last-resort; prefer rollback + routing adjustments.

End of note.

-- Aisha (on-call, afternoon rotation).
